svg.title: How the WooCommerce container resolves a class
svg.desc: Code in the includes directory calls wc_get_container and asks the Container for a class such as FeaturesController. The Container hands the request to the RuntimeContainer, which checks its cache, refuses classes outside the Automattic WooCommerce namespace, hands classes in the StoreApi and Blocks namespaces to the Blocks container, and otherwise uses reflection: it creates the object with a constructor that has no required arguments, then calls the public init method and passes it instances of the classes named by the type hints of its parameters, resolved the same way. Each instance is cached, so every caller receives the same object. Errors become a ContainerException. The Blocks container is a separate registry with explicit register and factory calls.">
svg.text: No registration list: every class in the Automattic\WooCommerce\ namespace is resolvable, built once and cached

explicit: $container->register( Id::class, closure ) builds a shared instance on first get(); factory( closure ) builds a new one every time
used by the Blocks bootstrap and by the Store API (routes, schemas, ExtendSchema). Extensions that extend the Store API call
StoreApi::container()->get( ExtendSchema::class ), never new ExtendSchema(), so that they share the one instance.
By convention, classes in src/ reach WordPress and includes/ through the two proxies, LegacyProxy and ActionsProxy, so they can be unit-tested.
